speaker: Snow leopard
prologue: I was born above the lights of Almaty.
My mother taught me every trail on this mountain.
Now I have a cub. This spring, I must teach him.

decisions.prompt: The people want a road up the mountain.

A.title: Cut the road straight through the gorge

B.title: Build it around — with a tunnel for animals

A: The trucks come at night. The lights blind us.
My cub hid behind me. We lost the trail to the high meadows.
B: They built a tunnel under the road for us.
My cub crossed it first. He wasn't afraid.

decisions.prompt: The people want snow for skiing.

A.title: Build the ski resort on her ridge

A: They took the ridge where my mother taught me to hunt.
There is nowhere to teach him now.
B: Today my cub caught his first pika. He was so proud.

decisions.prompt: Men came with guns. They want my fur.

A.title: No money for rangers this year

A: No one was watching the trails.
I heard the shot. I ran with my cub until morning.
B: Rangers walk the trails now. Cameras watch for us.
The men saw the cameras and went home.

decisions.prompt: I was hungry. I took a sheep from a herder.

A.title: Let the herder deal with it

B.title: Give him a strong pen and pay for the sheep

A: Now the herder is waiting for me with a gun.
I can't go down anymore. I can't feed my cub.
B: The people gave him a strong pen and paid for the sheep.
He let me pass. Tonight, my cub and I ate.

bright: He is grown now. He walks the trails I taught him.
One day he will teach his own cub.
Thank you for letting us stay.
middle: My cub left to find mountains without lights.
I am still here. For now.
faded: If you come here one day, look for our tracks in the snow.

bridge: That was a story. But the choices are real — and people have already made them.

ending.title: What people really did
ending.note: A simplified story, not a scientific prediction.
